source: Trane Technologies press release: Trane Technologies and Eaton Collaborate on Industry-First (08-17-2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Trane Technologies and Eaton announced a strategic collaboration integrating thermal management and electrical system architectures in a reference design (described by the companies as first-of-its kind) for higher-power-density AI factories, built in alignment with the NVIDIA DSX platforms. The design advances medium-voltage architectures and, versus conventional low-voltage designs, can achieve combined energy efficiency gains of up to 15%, cut copper use by as much as 80% and reduce installation costs by up to 30%, according to the companies. It is included in both the Trane Continuum Rubin DSX and Eaton Beam Rubin DSX platforms, with Eaton's technology helping provide power distribution for the Trane platform, and is designed to evolve as liquid cooling and direct current architectures become mainstream. CTO Mauro J. Atalla: combining Trane's thermal management with Eaton's power management delivers 'a coordinated design that helps customers accelerate deployment, improve efficiency and confidently plan to scale'.
quarterly_data.figure: energy efficiency gains of up to 15%; copper use cut by as much as 80%; installation costs reduced by up to 30%
